title: Unit 03: Book-II Prose Part 3 (Financial Career, China, Hunger & Population)
subject: english-12

questions.question: In 'My Financial Career', what psychological effect does entering a bank have on Stephen Leacock?

options.A: It fills him with civic pride and financial ambition.
options.B: The clerks, the wickets, and the sight of money rattle and intimidate him completely.
options.C: It makes him want to rob the vault.
options.D: It leaves him entirely unaffected.

questions.explanation: Leacock humorously confesses that the moment he crosses the threshold of a bank, everything—from the clerks to the wickets—rattles him into an idiot.

questions.question: How much money did Leacock intend to deposit when he nervously entered the bank?

options.A: Fifty-six dollars
options.B: Five thousand dollars
options.C: Fifty-six pounds
options.D: One hundred dollars

questions.explanation: His salary had been raised to fifty dollars a month, and he felt the bank was the only place for his massive savings of fifty-six dollars.

questions.question: Why did the bank manager usher Leacock into his private inner room with solemn secrecy?

options.A: He suspected Leacock was an international diamond smuggler.
options.B: Because Leacock whispered that he wished to speak with the manager 'alone', making him believe he was a Baron Rothschild or a Pinkerton detective.
options.C: Because the lobby was being renovated.
options.D: To offer him an executive vice-presidency.

questions.explanation: Leacock's mysterious, conspiratorial tone led the manager to assume he was an enormously wealthy capitalist or a private detective.

questions.question: What disastrous blunder did Leacock commit when writing out a cheque to withdraw six dollars for immediate spending?

options.A: He signed the manager's name instead of his own.
options.B: In his flustered state, he wrote 'fifty-six dollars' instead of six, withdrawing every single cent he had just deposited.
options.C: He dropped ink onto the teller's spectacles.
options.D: He made the cheque payable to the President of the United States.

questions.explanation: Paralyzed by embarrassment, he wrote fifty-six instead of six, and was too proud to admit his blunder, pretending he was insulted by the bank.

questions.question: Where does Leacock keep his money after his traumatic experience at the bank?

options.A: In a Swiss numbered deposit box
options.B: Cash in his trousers pocket and savings silver in a sock under his mattress
options.C: Invested in Wall Street stocks
options.D: In a safe at the local post office

questions.explanation: He vows never to bank again, keeping his cash in his trousers pocket and his savings tucked safely inside a sock.

questions.question: In 'China's Way to Progress', Galeazzo Santini highlights that the Chinese economic miracle was achieved without:

options.A: Massive foreign loans or subservience to western consumerist models
options.B: Hard physical labor by citizens
options.C: Any agricultural production
options.D: Universal literacy

questions.explanation: China relied on indigenous self-reliance, social discipline, and collective mobilization rather than foreign debt or western capitalist structures.

questions.question: What was the role of the 'barefoot doctors' in rural China as documented by Santini?

options.A: Specialized brain surgeons working without footwear in hospitals
options.B: Peasant healthcare workers trained in basic first aid, hygiene, and common remedies who treated farm workers directly in the fields
options.C: Religious shamans offering herbal incantations
options.D: Western medical tourists visiting Beijing

questions.explanation: Barefoot doctors were agricultural workers given rudimentary medical training to handle preventive medicine and minor ailments among peasant communes.

questions.question: How did Chinese society transform the status of women after the 1949 revolution?

options.A: By banning women from all economic activity
options.B: By granting women equal wages, eliminating female infanticide, abolishing arranged child marriages, and encouraging active political leadership
options.C: By forcing women into monastic seclusion
options.D: By exempting women from learning to read

questions.explanation: Under the slogan 'Women hold up half the sky', women attained full legal equality, paid maternity leave, and equal wages in communes.

questions.question: What is the administrative unit of agricultural production in Maoist China known as?

options.A: The People's Commune (split into Production Brigades and Production Teams)
options.B: The Feudal Manorial Estate
options.C: The Corporate Agribusiness Conglomerate
options.D: The Private Tenant Guild

questions.explanation: Communes organized rural labor democratically, coordinating farming, schooling, irrigation, and local militia.

questions.question: In 'Hunger and Population Explosion', Anna McKenzie notes that a major historical cause of famine was:

options.A: Excessive production of synthetic fertilizers
options.B: Crop failure due to drought, floods, or blight, coupled with total lack of transport to bring food from surplus regions
options.C: Strict government calorie rations
options.D: Overpopulation of wild animals eating grains

questions.explanation: Famines historically occurred when weather destroyed crops and isolated communities had no mechanical transport to import grain.

questions.question: What devastating plant disease caused the famous Irish Potato Famine of 1845–1847?

options.A: Potato blight fungus (Phytophthora infestans)
options.B: Wheat rust
options.C: Locust swarms
options.D: Apple scab

questions.explanation: The potato blight wiped out Ireland's staple crop, leading to over a million deaths from starvation and massive emigration to North America.

questions.question: What is the primary engine of the modern global 'population explosion' according to McKenzie?

options.A: A sudden, massive increase in the biological birth rate
options.B: A steep and dramatic drop in the death rate—especially infant mortality—brought about by modern medicine, antibiotics, and public sanitation
options.C: Global immigration to Mars
options.D: Government subsidies for large families in western Europe

questions.explanation: The population boom is not caused by women having more babies, but by medical science keeping infants alive and extending human longevity.

questions.question: What stark inequality between developed and developing nations is emphasized in 'Hunger and Population'?

options.A: Western citizens consume far more protein and grain, while billions in underdeveloped nations suffer chronic malnutrition and stunted growth.
options.B: Underdeveloped nations have too much food while Europe faces famine.
options.C: Developing nations have no agricultural land.
options.D: Western countries have completely stopped farming.

questions.explanation: Rich countries grapple with obesity and surplus grain, whereas poor countries suffer from severe caloric deficits and child malnutrition.

questions.question: In Leacock's essay, why did the accountant look at him with cold detachment?

options.A: He recognized Leacock from an unpaid grocery bill.
options.B: The accountant was a tall, cool devil whose very presence intensified Leacock's nervous tremors.
options.C: He thought Leacock had forged a cheque.
options.D: He was deaf and couldn't hear Leacock.

questions.explanation: Leacock describes the accountant as a tall, cool devil who treated his small deposit with indifferent routine.

questions.question: What did the bank clerks do as Leacock rushed headlong out of the bank doors?

options.A: They called the police armed with batons.
options.B: A roar of collective laughter echoed through the vaulted ceiling of the bank.
options.C: They locked the vault doors in panic.
options.D: They ran after him to return his hat.

questions.explanation: As the revolving doors swung behind him, a deafening roar of laughter went up from the clerks who realized his hilarious mistake.

questions.question: In Santini's description of Chinese cities, what striking absence distinguishes them from Western metropolises?

options.A: An absence of commercial advertising, neon signs, luxury private cars, and drug epidemics
options.B: An absence of streets and sidewalks
options.C: A complete lack of trees and parks
options.D: No people walking outdoors

questions.explanation: Chinese cities were characterized by sea of bicycles, simple clothing, and an absence of corporate billboards, glamour, and street vice.

questions.question: What does the Chinese concept of 'iron rice bowl' traditionally signify?

options.A: A literal utensil forged from iron ore in backyard furnaces
options.B: Guaranteed state employment, housing, healthcare, and food security for every working citizen
options.C: A military medal awarded to decorated soldiers
options.D: A tax levied on wheat production

questions.explanation: The 'iron rice bowl' represented the socialist guarantee of lifelong employment, food, and basic necessities.

questions.question: According to McKenzie, if global population continues to expand unchecked, the world will inevitably face:

options.A: Catastrophic resource depletion, water scarcity, environmental collapse, and widespread conflict
options.B: Universal peace and brotherhood
options.C: A sudden reduction in carbon emissions
options.D: An expansion of agricultural land into the oceans

questions.explanation: Uncontrolled exponential population growth threatens arable land, fresh water supplies, and geopolitical stability.

questions.question: What is the grammatical term for the underlined construction: 'Entering the bank, my hands began to tremble'?

options.A: Correct absolute clause
options.B: Dangling participle (illogical modifier, as hands cannot enter a bank)
options.C: Gerundial noun phrase
options.D: Infinitive of purpose

questions.explanation: The subject of the main clause ('hands') is not the agent of 'entering', making it a classic dangling modifier error.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct revision for the dangling modifier above?

options.A: As I entered the bank, my hands began to tremble.
options.B: Entering the bank, trembling occurred to my hands.
options.C: To enter the bank, my hands were trembling.
options.D: My hands entering the bank trembled.

questions.explanation: Revising into an adverbial clause with 'I' as the explicit subject clarifies the actor of the action.

questions.question: What is the tone of Stephen Leacock's 'My Financial Career'?

options.A: Tragic and remorseful
options.B: Farce, burlesque, and high comedy
options.C: Scholarly economics critique
options.D: Philosophical meditation

questions.explanation: Leacock is Canada's celebrated humorist, using farce and self-mockery to expose ordinary human nervousness.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'ghastly' in the sentence: 'He had a ghastly pale face'?

options.A: Extremely pleasant and cheerful
options.B: Deathly, frightfully pale or shocking
options.C: Sunburned and radiant
options.D: Intelligent and expressive

questions.explanation: 'Ghastly' means causing horror, resembling a ghost, or deathly pale.

questions.question: What was China's official policy regarding decentralization of industry as noted by Santini?

options.A: Forcing all factories into the capital city of Beijing
options.B: Encouraging rural communes to establish their own small-scale workshops and fertilizer plants to avoid mega-city congestion
options.C: Importing all industrial machinery from Japan
options.D: Closing all factories to return to ancient handicraft

questions.explanation: China dispersed production across rural areas, enabling farming brigades to build farm implements locally without overcrowding cities.

questions.question: In 'Hunger and Population', what biblical reference illustrates ancient famines?

options.A: The seven lean years of famine in Egypt interpreted by Joseph
options.B: The building of Noah's Ark
options.C: The destruction of Babylon
options.D: David and Goliath

questions.explanation: Pharaoh's dream of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean cows is cited as an ancient recorded famine in Egypt.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the idiom 'to face the music'?

options.A: To listen to an orchestral symphony
options.B: To confront unpleasant consequences or criticism for one's actions with courage
options.C: To dance at a celebration
options.D: To play an instrument in public

questions.explanation: 'Facing the music' means bravely confronting the repercussions or penalties of one's blunders.

questions.question: Why did Leacock insist on pretending that someone had insulted him when withdrawing all his money?

options.A: To save face and mask his embarrassing blunder behind a façade of righteous indignation
options.B: Because the teller had actually insulted his mother
options.C: Because the money was counterfeit
options.D: To sue the bank for slander

questions.explanation: Rather than confessing that he had made a foolish mathematical error on the cheque, he feigned outrage to look purposeful.

questions.question: What does the demographic term 'infant mortality rate' measure?

options.A: The number of babies born in private hospitals
options.B: The number of deaths of infants under one year old per 1,000 live births in a given year
options.C: The percentage of children attending primary school
options.D: The number of pediatricians per city

questions.explanation: Infant mortality is a primary barometer of public health, measuring baby deaths per thousand live births.

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'I opened an account here yesterday.'

options.A: He said that he opened an account here yesterday.
options.B: He said that he had opened an account there the day before.
options.C: He said he has opened an account there yesterday.
options.D: He said that he opens an account there tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Past simple shifts to past perfect ('had opened'), 'here' shifts to 'there', and 'yesterday' shifts to 'the day before'.

questions.question: In 'China's Way to Progress', the phrase 'reliance on the masses' emphasizes:

options.A: Relying on foreign tourists for tax revenue
options.B: Trusting the collective wisdom, enthusiasm, and labor of ordinary working people rather than an elite bureaucracy
options.C: Subsidizing imports of luxury cars
options.D: Replacing manual labor with automated robotics

questions.explanation: Maoist philosophy highlighted the creative capacity and collective spirit of the common workers and peasants.

questions.question: What is the synonym of 'indolence' in student behavior?

options.A: Sloth, laziness, or inactivity
options.B: Keen curiosity
options.C: Sharp mathematical precision
options.D: Physical strength

questions.explanation: 'Indolence' is habitual laziness, sluggishness, or avoidance of physical/mental exertion.

questions.question: Identify the sentence that uses the correct idiom:

options.A: He burned the midnight oil to prepare for his exams.
options.B: He boiled the midnight kerosene for his exams.
options.C: He lit the evening candle for his exams.
options.D: He roasted the midnight lamp for his exams.

questions.explanation: The correct English idiom for studying late into the night is 'to burn the midnight oil'.

questions.question: In 'Hunger and Population', what does McKenzie describe as the tragic irony of food distribution?

options.A: Food cannot be transported over oceans.
options.B: Global grain production is technically sufficient to feed humanity, yet economic barriers leave millions starving while rich nations destroy surpluses to maintain prices.
options.C: All humans eat identical amounts of grain.
options.D: Developing nations have no rivers.

questions.explanation: Famine in the modern world is fundamentally an issue of poverty, logistics, and unequal wealth rather than sheer global food absence.

questions.question: In Leacock's essay, how did the manager react when Leacock confessed he only had $56 to deposit?

options.A: He stood up coldly, opened the door, and called out to the accountant in icy disdain.
options.B: He embraced Leacock with tears of joy.
options.C: He offered to double his money.
options.D: He called the armed guards.

questions.explanation: Realizing his private time had been wasted by a nervous clerk with $56, the manager's cordiality vanished into chilly contempt.

questions.question: What is the antonym of 'opulence' as contrasted with Chinese austerity?

options.A: Poverty / Penury / Frugality
options.B: Luxury
options.C: Wealth
options.D: Affluence

questions.explanation: 'Opulence' signifies great wealth, luxury, and lavishness; its antonym is frugality, simplicity, or poverty.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences exhibits correct subject-verb agreement?

options.A: Each of the commune workers receives their ration vouchers daily.
options.B: Each of the commune workers receives his ration voucher daily.
options.C: Each of the commune workers receive their ration vouchers daily.
options.D: Each of the commune workers are receiving their ration vouchers daily.

questions.explanation: 'Each' is an indefinite pronoun that takes singular verbs ('receives') and singular possessive pronouns ('his').
